title: Pneumonia, lung abscess, empyema and respiratory arrest in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the main lung condition (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/16/2026
Reason for Admission: Community-acquired pneumonia

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 76, Temp 98.9 F, SpO2 96% on room air.
Recent Labs: WBC 11.4 x 10^9/L, Hemoglobin 14.2 g/dL, Platelets 210 x 10^3/uL, Creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, eGFR 92 mL/min/1.73m2.

Social History: Lives with spouse. Former smoker (quit 5 years ago). No alcohol use.
Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had diabetes.
Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Positive for fever, chills, and fatigue.
Respiratory: Positive for cough and shortness of breath.
Cardiovascular: Negative for chest pain.
Gastrointestinal: Negative for nausea or diarrhea.
Neurological: Negative for headache or confusion.

History of Present Illness:
Patient is a 55-year-old male presenting with a 3-day history of productive cough, productive of yellow sputum, and associated with subjective fevers and pleuritic chest pain. He reports significant shortness of breath when walking short distances.

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted for management of community-acquired pneumonia. Initial workup included a chest X-ray which confirmed an infiltrate. Sputum and blood cultures were obtained; however, cultures were negative and no organism was identified. The patient was started on a course of intravenous antibiotics. He tolerated the treatment well, showing significant improvement in oxygen saturation and a decrease in productive cough. He remained afebrile for 48 hours and was transitioned to oral medications prior to discharge.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Community-acquired pneumonia

Discharge Medications:
Amoxicillin 500mg PO every 8 hours for 7 days.
Guaifenesin 600mg PO every 4 hours as needed for cough.

Follow-up:
Patient to follow up with primary care physician in 10 days for a repeat chest X-ray to ensure resolution of pneumonia.

Electronically signed, J. Lindqvist, MD, 05/16/2026
explanations: Pneumonia with no organism identified: J18.9 (no HCC).
